\paragraph{Cross-model transfer.}
The high cross-model retention among continuation-mode generators (Pythia$\leftrightarrow$OLMo: 90--92\%, Qwen-cont$\leftrightarrow$Pythia: 84--85\%) implies that a classifier trained on one generator's depth chain can generalize to corpora from unknown generators within the same generation mode.
This scorer-agnostic property is essential for deployment on web-crawled corpora where the generating model is unidentified: a single trained OBD classifier can serve as a portable depth estimator without retraining.
Feature ranking stability across scorers ($\rho > 0.90$) reinforces this conclusion, as the same statistical signatures dominate regardless of the scoring model.
The poor transfer from rewrite-mode classifiers (61--63\%) isolates generation mode as the primary source of distributional variation, exceeding the effect of architecture family; practitioners should verify the generation mode of their target corpus before applying cross-model depth estimation.
